1.0.0.en: The Apostle begins his discourse by presenting himself as an apostle of Jesus Christ by the call and will of God. He did not appoint himself an apostle, as those who opposed him in Corinth claimed. He also sends them the greeting of Sosthenes, whom he regards as his brother, who had formerly been a ruler of a synagogue of the Jews and then became a Christian.

1.1.0.en: By calling them the Church of God, he reveals that the Church is possessed by the Lord. As for naming churches after the saints, this is to honor them and to distinguish the churches from one another because of their number. He calls them sanctified in Christ Jesus, set apart from the Gentiles and dedicated to God. That is, the Lord chose us Christians to be His own and to be called by His name.

1.2.0.en: Finally, he grants them the apostolic blessing, which is grace, that is, the gift of God, and peace as the fruit of grace.

1.2.1.en: If you pray and call upon the name of Christ, be confident that you receive grace and peace. So take care to begin your day and end it with prayer, to take refuge in God in every affliction and to thank Him for all His gifts; for as much as your day is filled with prayer, your heart is filled with peace.

1.3.s.en: (2) Steadfastness in the faith and readiness

1.3.0.en: The Apostle thanks God for the gifts He gave to the believers of Corinth, like the rest of the believers, which were given to them through their union with Jesus Christ, so that they became rich in the understanding of the message of the Gospel. They also stood firm in the faith in the salvation that Christ accomplished and that the Apostles preached to them, and they remained steadfast in their faith by enduring persecutions and torments even to the point of martyrdom.

1.4.0.en: Their church is filled with spiritual gifts, which help in its edification and its readiness for the second coming of Christ.

1.5.0.en: The Lord Jesus Christ will confirm them in the faith to the end of their life on earth, so that there will be nothing in them for which they could be blamed on the day of judgment.

1.6.0.en: God is faithful in His call to them, for He will bring them into the life of fellowship in His Son Jesus Christ our Lord.

1.6.1.en: Looking to the heavenly Kingdom makes you hold fast to your faith, your prayers and your church, and bind yourself to your fellow believers. Thus you grow in the love of God and make light of the desires of the world, and also of its cares and toils; rather, you experience the love of God every day and long to be with Him.

1.7.0.en: "Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you; but that ye be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment." The Apostle calls them brethren, for all Christians, in the fellowship of the blood of Christ, have become brethren in one body, whose head is Christ and whose members are the members of the Church. So when we divide among ourselves and quarrel with one another, it is as if we were dividing the one body of Christ. How hard that is on the heart of Christ, because of the disturbance it brings to the one Church and the stumbling blocks it causes! This also shows the humility of Paul, who had the right to call them my children or my sons, for he was their bishop and their father, yet he called them brethren.

1.8.0.en: For it has been declared to me by those of the house of Chloe, a woman well known to the Christians of Corinth, that there are contentions among you which have led you into division.

1.9.0.en: Among you are those who say that they follow Paul and form factions for him; others follow Apollos, who was a Jew who became a Christian, an Alexandrian learned in the Scriptures and concerned with interpretation; a group who admired his eloquence followed him and formed factions for him. Among you are those who follow Cephas (the Jewish name of Peter) and form factions for him, and among you are those who set up a party and called themselves the party of Christ.

1.10.0.en: The Apostle affirms, in the form of questions, that Christ is one and was crucified for all, and that no one else redeemed them, not even Paul, and that they were not baptized in his name.

1.10.1.en: The word "in the name" in Greek means Christ's ownership of the one baptized and his union with Him. In the Liturgy of St. Gregory, in the first litany, the Church reminds us to pray all together, asking for oneness of heart and the ending of the divisions of the Church.

1.10.2.en: The Apostle asks the believers to have the mind of Christ, that is, one mind (ch. 2:16).

1.11.0.en: The Apostle thanks God that he baptized none of them but Crispus, who was a ruler of a Jewish synagogue and believed through the hand of the Apostle Paul, and Gaius, who was a Christian who hosted the meetings of the Church in his house, and himself Paul, so that no one should say that he had baptized in his own name. He also baptized the household of Stephanas; beyond that, he does not mention that he baptized anyone else. The Apostle is not concerned to baptize personally, because his chief work as a bishop is preaching under the guidance of the Holy Spirit and not with the philosophy of the world.

1.11.1.en: Hold your own opinion even if it differs from others, for differing opinions complete one another; but beware of divisions, for they carry pride and lack of love. Do not oppose in order to show yourself off, but be diligent for peace and unity.

1.12.s.en: (4) The Cross is the power and the wisdom of God

1.12.0.en: The Cross of Christ, in the eyes of unbelievers, who will perish because of their unbelief, is a kind of foolishness, because it shows the weakness of Christ. But to us, who are saved by the work of the Cross, it is the power of God, which transfers us from the death of sin to life in Christ.

1.13.0.en: It is written (in Isa 29:14) that by the divine wisdom, in accomplishing salvation by the Cross, the Lord made void all the human wisdom of the wise, which was unable to set man right; therefore the Church took the Cross as a symbol of salvation.

1.14.0.en: The Apostle asks a rhetorical question in order to expose the failure of the Jews and the philosophers of the Gentiles, with all their wisdom, knowledge and ability to debate, to repair the corruption that had befallen man.

1.15.0.en: The world could not know God through His wisdom, which is clearly declared in all creation, so He was pleased to save them from sin by what He accomplished by His death on the Cross, which unbelievers regard as foolishness.

1.16.0.en: For the Jews seek a mighty, powerful savior who does miraculous works, and the Greeks seek a savior marked by philosophy and wisdom. Therefore our preaching of Christ crucified is not accepted by the Jews, who were awaiting salvation from the Romans and not from sin, and it contradicts the wisdom of the Greeks, who regard the preaching of the Cross as foolishness.

1.17.0.en: As for us believers, whether we are Jews or Greeks, we have recognized the power of God and the wisdom of God in accomplishing salvation by the Cross.

1.18.0.en: What seems to others to be foolishness has accomplished for mankind what their wisdom was unable to accomplish, and what seems to be weakness in the Cross has accomplished the salvation that all human powers were unable to accomplish.

1.18.1.en: Receive the word of God with faith and submission so that you may apply it in your life and it may work in you, and reject doubts or any thought that is not edifying, however logical it may appear.

1.19.0.en: "For ye see your calling, brethren": consider the Lord's call to you, that it was not based on any human wisdom you had, or the power of your social standing, or your family and lineage, as proved by the fact that there are not many among you who have wisdom, or power, or nobility of birth.

1.20.0.en: God chose the simple, whom people regard as weak and ignorant, yet His work appeared clearly in their lives by their acceptance of the salvation which others, wise in their own eyes, were unable to understand.

1.21.0.en: God also chose those who are weak in their standing and lineage, and "base things", that is, those who are not of the upper class in society, and "things which are despised", that is, those held in contempt in the eyes of people, and "things which are not", that is, those who have no account among people, in order to bring to nothing, by their salvation, the arguments of all the prominent in society. This was made clear in the Lord's choice of His disciples and apostles, most of whom were from the simple class in society.

1.22.0.en: This is so that those who have human power or wisdom may be certain that salvation does not come by power or wisdom.

1.23.0.en: "Of Him are ye in Christ Jesus": it is from Christ that your call came, to life with Him and to receiving wisdom, righteousness and sanctification.

1.24.0.en: So let our boasting be in the Lord, for all our abilities are a gift from Him, and by this we are saved from pride.

1.24.1.en: God is ready to work through you however weak you may be. So trust in His power and seek the salvation of those around you; and as much as you thank God, His grace increases in you.

1.24.2.en: The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians. Spiritual wisdom

2.0.s.en: (1) Preaching with the wisdom of the Holy Spirit

2.0.0.en: The Apostle Paul reminds them that when he preached the Gospel to them he did not rely on eloquence and philosophy, but concentrated his speech on the story of the salvation accomplished by Jesus Christ on the Cross, whose effect on everyone who hears it surpasses in power any eloquence of expression.

2.0.1.en: Do not rely, in persuading others, on your philosophy and your own abilities, but through prayer receive grace to present your words in a simple and convincing way. And if God wishes, He will guide you by using the various means of persuasion, so that your reliance is on God in everything.

2.1.0.en: The Apostle Paul means that he did not preach Christ relying on any human ability or power; on the contrary, his sense of the weight of the responsibility put him in a state of great fear.

2.2.0.en: Likewise he did not preach to them relying on human wisdom and rhetorical, rational persuasion, but relied on the powerful guidance of the Holy Spirit.

2.3.0.en: This was so that all might know that the credit for their faith does not belong to rational proofs, but to the divine power that is able to establish them in the faith.

2.3.1.en: It is good that you appreciate the weight of the responsibility upon you, and pray, asking for God's help, and carry out the work with care because you are liable to error, and accept the guidance of others and their completing of what you do.

2.4.0.en: The Apostle Paul goes on to say that he speaks among those who are spiritually mature a wisdom that is not of this world, that is, not an invention of men or of the great ones of the world, whose destiny is to come to an end.

2.5.0.en: Paul speaks the wisdom of God which He declared in the Gospel, which is like a mystery to unbelievers. The mystery here is everything that was declared in the Gospel concerning the matters of redemption by Jesus Christ, for they cannot grasp it, because it is the wisdom hidden from the human mind; although God prepared it from eternity, He did not declare it until this age, so that we might have a share in eternal glory.

2.6.0.en: The great ones of the world cannot attain this wisdom, for had they known that Christ is the Son of God, they would not have dared to crucify Him.

2.6.1.en: So we Christians must not boast of our earthly wisdom, but rather strive to be filled with the divine wisdom which the Holy Spirit gives us, as the Apostle James said, that if we ever have bitter envying and strife in our hearts, we should know that this wisdom does not descend from above.

2.7.s.en: (2) The work of the Holy Spirit

2.7.0.en: Here the Apostle speaks of the eternal glory that God has prepared for us, which surpasses everything our senses can grasp. No one can imagine it, and no human being has ever seen it or heard of it. So we too must choose between the spiritual perfection that leads us to eternal glory, and vain greatness that causes envy and strife.

2.8.0.en: By the Spirit we can sense the majesty of this glory through what God reveals to us by His Holy Spirit, who knows all that is God's.

2.9.0.en: To clarify this idea, the Apostle sets man before us as an example. Just as the spirit of man knows his intentions and the thoughts of his heart, so also the Spirit of God knows all the things of God and declares them to us.

2.10.0.en: The spiritual things that are revealed by the Holy Spirit we know from the Holy Spirit who dwells in us, which is impossible for the people of the world, in whom the Spirit of God does not dwell. For we, by Baptism and the Holy Myron, have had the Holy Spirit descend upon us, and have become qualified to receive the gifts and fruits of the Holy Spirit.

2.10.1.en: So let us take care not to "quench the Spirit", but practice the spiritual means so that we may grow in the Spirit.

2.11.0.en: The Apostle goes on to say: We too, when we speak of these things in our preaching, do not use human wisdom to convey their meanings to people, but draw wisdom from the Holy Spirit who dwells in us, and so use spiritual expressions to present spiritual concepts. It is not right that spiritual things be judged by earthly, temporal measures and standards.

2.11.1.en: The Holy Spirit who dwells in you is able to search the depths of God. How great are these blessings, because through them you can grow in your prayers and enjoy communion with God, and also understand and delight in His word in the Holy Bible. For God wants to bring you into His embrace, that you may be united with Him and rejoice in being always with Him. So ask for the help of the Holy Spirit in all your spiritual practices, and you will be filled with vitality and a sense of God.

2.12.s.en: (3) The mind of the spiritual man

2.12.0.en: The natural man, who is the man who lives in material things and judges matters by a material measure, finds it impossible to accept spiritual things; indeed, the teachings of the Holy Spirit are considered by him wrong and unsound, because knowing these things requires a spiritual knowledge entirely higher than the limits of his human knowledge.

2.13.0.en: The spiritual man has, beyond his material abilities, spiritual abilities, which he receives from the Holy Spirit who dwells in him, so that he is able to discern not only fleshly matters but spiritual ones as well. Therefore it is not the right of the man who has only human abilities to judge the spiritual man; for how can he judge spiritual matters that do not at all fall within the scope of his fleshly knowledge? On the contrary, the spiritual man easily discerns and judges all those around him.

2.13.1.en: The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians

2.14.0.en: He who knows the mind of the Lord is able to teach it to others and to judge among them on the basis of this mind. Therefore the natural man, who does not know the mind of Christ, has no right to teach us and to judge us, who in fact have the mind of Christ.

2.14.1.en: To have the mind of Christ means to see things as Christ sees them and to measure them by the measure by which Christ measures. So the Apostle wants to say that the judgment of the philosophers that my teaching is ignorance is a false judgment that carries no weight.

2.14.2.en: Do not be disturbed by the objections of those far from the Church to your spiritual conduct, but stand firm in your life with God, submissive to the guidance of your father of confession and your spiritual guides, and ask for the guidance of the Holy Spirit to understand the right conduct with all those around you.

2.14.3.en: The servant, the ministry and salvation
